title: Residual-certified mass through preparation and clean projection
author: /root/batch2_composition
question:
Let \(n\ge 0\) and let \(r_0,\ldots,r_n\) be finite nonnegative bond dimensions with \(r_0=r_n=1\). For \(j=1,\ldots,n\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(A_j^t\) be a real \(r_{j-1}\)-by-\(r_j\) matrix. The raw vector \(x\in\mathbb R^{2^n}\) has coordinates
\[
x_s=(A_1^{s_1}\cdots A_n^{s_n})_{1,1},
\]
with one empty word and empty product \(I_1\) when \(n=0\). Use Euclidean vector norms and their induced operator norms. Write
\[
T_j(Z)=\sum_{t=0}^1 A_j^t Z(A_j^t)^{\mathsf T},\qquad
E_n=I_1,\qquad E_{j-1}=T_j(E_j).
\]
You may use the exact Gram identity \(E_0(1,1)=\lVert x\rVert^2\).

Suppose supplied real matrices \(\widehat E_j\) of size \(r_j\)-by-\(r_j\) satisfy \(\widehat E_n=I_1\), and supplied nonnegative certificates \(\varepsilon_j,L_j\) obey
\[
\lVert\widehat E_{j-1}-T_j(\widehat E_j)\rVert\le\varepsilon_j,
\qquad \sum_t\lVert A_j^t\rVert^2\le L_j.
\]
No positivity or canonicality of the \(\widehat E_j\) or the cores is assumed. Derive an explicit a posteriori number \(\beta\), in terms of the \(\varepsilon_j,L_j\), with
\[
\bigl|\widehat E_0(1,1)-\lVert x\rVert^2\bigr|\le\beta.
\]
Give the \(n=0\) convention. Explain why propagation factors from preceding cores cannot in general be omitted; exhibit a scalar-bond example in which replacing \(\beta\) by \(\sum_j\varepsilon_j\) would falsely certify positive mass for the zero raw vector.

For the remainder use your certified \(m:=\widehat E_0(1,1)-\beta\) and assume \(m>0\). A second raw vector \(y\in\mathbb R^{2^n}\) satisfies \(\lVert x-y\rVert\le\delta\), where \(0\le\delta<\sqrt m\). Prove \(x\) and \(y\) nonzero before defining \(\psi=x/\lVert x\rVert\) and \(\phi=y/\lVert y\rVert\). You may use the supplied normalization inequality
\[
\left\lVert\frac{u}{\lVert u\rVert}-\frac{v}{\lVert v\rVert}\right\rVert
\le\frac{2\lVert u-v\rVert}{\lVert u\rVert}
\]
for nonzero finite real or complex vectors \(u,v\).

Let \(H=\mathbb C^{2^n}\), \(K=\mathbb C^{2^a}\) with \(a\ge0\), \(Jv=|0^a\rangle\otimes v\), and \(P=JJ^\dagger\), in the fixed order \(K\otimes H\). All workspace is included in \(K\). Two actual unitary gate lists \(U\) and \(V\) have the same length, instruction types and physical targets in every position; only Y-rotation angles differ. A rotation is
\[
R(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\theta/2)&-\sin(\theta/2)\\ \sin(\theta/2)&\cos(\theta/2)\end{pmatrix},
\]
and the supplied angle error at rotation occurrence \(k\) is \(d_k\ge0\). All other gates agree exactly, including phases. Chronological products place the first gate rightmost. You may use the supplied aligned-circuit bound
\[
\lVert V-U\rVert\le\gamma:=\frac12\sum_k d_k.
\]
The exact preparation action is \(U|0^{a+n}\rangle=J\phi\).

For \(\Omega=V|0^{a+n}\rangle\) and \(\tau:=2\delta/\sqrt m+\gamma\), derive a full-output bound relative to \(J\psi\). Assume \(\tau<1\) before conditioning. Decompose \(\Omega\) into clean and rejected branches, prove the clean branch is nonzero, and prove that its success probability \(p\) and normalized accepted system vector \(\psi_{\mathrm{acc}}\) satisfy
\[
p\ge(1-\tau^2/2)^2,\qquad
\lVert\psi_{\mathrm{acc}}-\psi\rVert\le\tau.
\]
In particular justify the conditional-vector bound from the unit norm of the full output; do not silently replace it by a phase-minimized distance. Explain why \(\tau<1\) is a sufficient rather than a claimed sharp threshold, and give a unitary example with zero clean success and full-output distance \(\sqrt2\) from a clean target.

Check zero residuals, zero data/gate errors, \(n=0\), \(a=0\), and an internal zero bond dimension. Keep cases that contradict \(m>0\) separate from the active normalization theorem. State exactly which conclusions depend on the certified residuals, raw-data error, and actual circuit action/alignment; no floating-point residual certifier, angle supplier, state-loading algorithm, finite-gate-set compiler, or runtime bound is supplied.
assumptions: Finite real scalar-boundary tensor train with fixed bit order; approximate Gram environments have exact terminal I_1 and certified local operator-norm residuals ε_j and transfer bounds L_j.
For the normalization/circuit branch only: m=Ē_0(1,1)−β>0 and ||x−y||≤δ<√m with δ≥0.
The actual unitary lists are positionally aligned, differing only in same-target half-angle Y rotations with certified errors d_k; all other instructions and exact phases agree.
After φ is proved well-defined, the exact list has complete output U|0^{a+n}⟩=Jφ, including clean workspace; τ=2δ/√m+γ<1 is imposed before conditional normalization.
Exact Gram, normalization stability and aligned-circuit norm bounds are supplied interfaces; residual propagation, margin checks and downstream projection estimates are to be derived.
conventions: All vector distances compare exact representatives. Complex inner products are conjugate-linear in the first argument; real vectors embed componentwise in H.
Registers are ordered ancilla/workspace K then system H; J is the clean isometry and success projects every qubit of K onto zero.
Empty products equal 1 and empty sums 0; a zero-qubit system is one-dimensional. Zero-dimensional internal bonds are allowed and force the raw contraction to vanish.
The false-certificate example and vanishing-mass cases are diagnostics outside the active m>0 branch. No normalization of a zero vector is defined.

reference_answer:
For any real matrix \(Z\) of the appropriate size, submultiplicativity and transpose invariance of the induced Euclidean operator norm give
\[
\lVert T_j(Z)\rVert\le\sum_t\lVert A_j^t\rVert^2\lVert Z\rVert\le L_j\lVert Z\rVert.
\]
The same estimate applies to \(T_j(Z-Z')\), since the transfer map is linear. No positivity, symmetry or canonicality of the approximate environments is used.

Set \(D_j=\widehat E_j-E_j\) and \(R_j=\widehat E_{j-1}-T_j(\widehat E_j)\). The terminal condition gives \(D_n=0\), and subtracting recurrences gives
\[
D_{j-1}=R_j+T_j(D_j),\qquad
\lVert D_{j-1}\rVert\le\varepsilon_j+L_j\lVert D_j\rVert.
\]
Define \(\beta_n=0\) and \(\beta_{j-1}=\varepsilon_j+L_j\beta_j\). Backward induction proves \(\lVert D_j\rVert\le\beta_j\), and expanding the scalar recurrence yields
\[
\boxed{\beta=\beta_0=\sum_{j=1}^n\varepsilon_j\prod_{k=1}^{j-1}L_k.}
\]
All factors are nonnegative. The first residual has coefficient \(1\); the second has \(L_1\); the last is amplified by \(L_1\cdots L_{n-1}\). The initial matrices are scalar, so their operator norm is the absolute value of their entry. With the supplied Gram identity,
\[
\bigl|\widehat E_0(1,1)-\lVert x\rVert^2\bigr|=\lVert D_0\rVert\le\beta.
\]
For \(n=0\), the sum is empty, \(\beta=0\), and \(E_0=\widehat E_0=I_1\). The single empty-word amplitude is \(1\).

The propagation weights cannot be discarded even when all approximate scalar environments are nonnegative. Take two scalar-bond cores
\[
A_1^0=2,\quad A_1^1=0,\quad A_2^0=A_2^1=0.
\]
Then \(x=0\), \(E_2=1\), and \(E_1=E_0=0\). Set
\[
(\widehat E_0,\widehat E_1,\widehat E_2)=(4,1,1),\quad
(L_1,L_2)=(4,0),\quad(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)=(0,1).
\]
These certificates hold: \(R_1=4-4\cdot1=0\) and \(R_2=1-0=1\). The correct \(\beta=4\) gives \(m=0\). Replacing it by \(\sum_j\varepsilon_j=1\) would falsely report positive mass \(4-1=3\) for the zero vector. This diagnostic does not satisfy the active \(m>0\) premise.

Now retain the active branch. The certified interval implies
\[
\lVert x\rVert\ge\sqrt m>0,\qquad
\lVert y\rVert\ge\lVert x\rVert-\lVert x-y\rVert
\ge\sqrt m-\delta>0.
\]
Thus both vectors are nonzero before normalization. The vectors \(\psi=x/\lVert x\rVert\) and \(\phi=y/\lVert y\rVert\) are unit, and the supplied stability inequality gives
\[
\lVert\phi-\psi\rVert\le\frac{2\lVert x-y\rVert}{\lVert x\rVert}
\le\frac{2\delta}{\sqrt m}.
\]
This retains signed real amplitudes as exact representatives.

Write \(\xi=|0^{a+n}\rangle\). The actual aligned-list estimate, the exact preparation action and the isometry of \(J\) give
\[
\Omega-J\psi=(V-U)\xi+J(\phi-\psi),\qquad
\lVert\Omega-J\psi\rVert\le\gamma+\frac{2\delta}{\sqrt m}=\tau.
\]
Independently, \(V\) is unitary, so \(\lVert\Omega\rVert=1\), while \(\lVert J\psi\rVert=1\). Both full-output norms matter below.

Set \(z=J^\dagger\Omega\) and \(\ell=(I-P)\Omega\). Since \(J^\dagger J=I\), the operator \(P=JJ^\dagger\) is an orthogonal projector and
\[
\Omega=Jz+\ell,\qquad J^\dagger\ell=0,\qquad
\lVert z\rVert^2+\lVert\ell\rVert^2=1.
\]
The Born success probability is \(p=\lVert z\rVert^2\). Put \(q=\lVert z\rVert\le1\) and \(h=\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi,z\rangle=\operatorname{Re}\langle J\psi,\Omega\rangle\). The squared distance of the full unit vectors gives
\[
2-2h=\lVert\Omega-J\psi\rVert^2\le\tau^2,
\qquad h\ge1-\tau^2/2>0.
\]
The final strict inequality uses \(\tau<1\). Cauchy–Schwarz then gives
\[
q\ge|\langle\psi,z\rangle|\ge h\ge1-\tau^2/2>0.
\]
The clean branch is therefore nonzero before conditioning, and
\[
\boxed{p=q^2\ge(1-\tau^2/2)^2.}
\]

The normalized accepted joint vector is \(J(z/q)\), so \(\psi_{\mathrm{acc}}=z/q\). Because \(h>0\) and \(q\le1\),
\[
\lVert\psi_{\mathrm{acc}}-\psi\rVert^2
=2-\frac{2h}{q}\le2-2h
=\lVert\Omega-J\psi\rVert^2\le\tau^2.
\]
Consequently \(\boxed{\lVert\psi_{\mathrm{acc}}-\psi\rVert\le\tau}\). This exact-representative argument does not minimize over phase. It also does not erase the rejected branch before measurement. The weaker leakage estimate \(\lVert\ell\rVert\le\tau\) would only yield \(p\ge1-\tau^2\); by itself it does not establish the stronger requested bounds.

The threshold \(\tau<1\) is sufficient. The same reasoning has \(h>0\) for every \(\tau<\sqrt2\), including \(\tau=1\), where it gives \(p\ge1/4\). A loose bound above \(1\) does not imply failure. For zero success at actual distance \(\sqrt2\), take \(n=0\), \(a=1\), \(x=y=(1)\), \(U=R(0)\) and \(V=R(\pi)\) on the sole ancilla. Then
\[
U|0\rangle=|0\rangle,\quad V|0\rangle=|1\rangle,\quad
P=|0\rangle\langle0|,\quad p=0,\quad
\lVert|1\rangle-|0\rangle\rVert=\sqrt2.
\]
The lists are aligned with \(d_1=\pi\) and conservative \(\gamma=\pi/2\), so this example deliberately lies outside the active \(\tau<1\) branch. Every unit vector perpendicular to the clean subspace has distance \(\sqrt2\) from every clean unit target.

If every residual certificate is zero, then \(\beta=0\) and the initial approximate entry is exact mass. That mass may still vanish; normalization continues to require \(m>0\). If \(\delta=0\), then \(y=x\). If \(\gamma=0\), then \(V=U\) in operator norm. If both errors vanish in the active branch, then \(\Omega=J\psi\), \(p=1\), and the accepted vector is exact. For \(n=0\), one has \(x=(1)\), \(\beta=0\), \(m=1\); the real scalar \(y\) is positive under \(\delta<1\), so \(\phi=\psi=(1)\). This is a one-dimensional system, not an empty vector. For \(a=0\), \(P=I\) and \(p=1\). A zero internal bond makes every full contraction zero; the certified interval forces \(m\le0\). It cannot satisfy the active normalization branch, and no zero vector is normalized.

The conclusion needs the complete conjunction of certified residuals and transfer bounds for the displayed exact cores, the Gram interpretation as the particular raw vector, positive certified mass, raw-data error to the particular second vector, complete exact preparation, actual unitary positional alignment and the specified projector. The proof constructs no floating-point residual certifier, rounded Gram algorithm, raw-data or norm supplier, preparation circuit, angle supplier, finite-gate-set compiler or runtime bound. The stored exact-real Gram source does not itself certify numerical residuals.

rubric.criterion: Proves the transfer bound, signed residual recurrence and backward induction, obtaining \(\beta=\sum_j\varepsilon_j\prod_{k<j}L_k\) with the correct product orientation and \(n=0\) convention. An unweighted or reversed product earns no propagation-formula credit.

Gives a legal concrete scalar-bond false-certificate example, verifies its residuals and transfer bounds, and shows that the unweighted positive mass is false while the correct certificate does not imply positivity.

Uses the Gram interpretation and \(m>0\) to establish \(x\ne0\), proves \(\lVert y\rVert\ge\sqrt m-\delta>0\) before normalization, and correctly invokes the supplied stability result. No proof of the supplied result is required.
Combines the actual action \(U\xi=J\phi\), aligned operator error and data-normalization error to obtain \(\lVert\Omega-J\psi\rVert\le\tau\), retaining complete workspace and full unit norms.

Derives the branch decomposition, uses positive real overlap \(h\ge1-\tau^2/2\) and \(q\le1\) to prove \(q>0\) before conditioning, and proves both \(p\ge(1-\tau^2/2)^2\) and accepted error at most \(\tau\). Equivalent complete geometric arguments earn full credit. The weaker \(1-\tau^2\) or \(2\tau\) bounds alone do not prove the requested conclusion.

Treats \(\tau<1\) as sufficient, supplies a unitary zero-success example at actual distance \(\sqrt2\) in a separate regime, and handles \(n=0\), \(a=0\), zero errors/residuals and internal zero bonds without contradictory positive-mass premises.

Keeps residual certification, raw error, actual complete preparation, alignment and projection as distinct required interfaces; distinguishes the mathematical estimate from an unprovided finite-bit supplier, compiler or runtime theorem.

common_errors.why_wrong: Residual at j is transported through T_1,...,T_{j−1}; large earlier cores can amplify it.

common_errors.error: Treat Ē_0≥0 or an approximate Gram matrix as automatically certifying positive true mass.
common_errors.why_wrong: Only Ē_0−β is a validated lower bound; approximate-environment positivity is neither given nor sufficient.

common_errors.error: Normalize y before proving nonvanishing, or use small absolute δ without a positive certified margin.
common_errors.why_wrong: The checked inequality δ<√m≤||x|| is the required nonzero producer.

common_errors.error: Replace actual circuit alignment with a generic assertion that angles are close.

common_errors.error: Apply a generic normalized-branch lemma to get only 2τ and claim it proves the requested τ bound.
common_errors.why_wrong: The sharper result uses both full-output unit norms and positive real overlap h, together with q≤1.

common_errors.error: Assert τ=1 allows zero success or import τ<1 into the √2 witness.
common_errors.why_wrong: τ<1 is sufficient, not sharp; the diagnostic replaces that premise.
